pr_title: Enhance `Lint/RedundantSafeNavigation` to handle conversion methods with defaults
pr_body:
Fixes #12412.

With these changes I found a few offenses in the gitlab's codebase.
pr_comments:
The example is missing:
```ruby
# bad
hsh&.to_h { |k, v| [k, v] } || {}
# good
hsh.to_h { |k, v| [k, v] }
```

> With these changes I found a few offenses in the gitlab's codebase.

This should fix the following offenses: https://github.com/gitlabhq/gitlabhq/blob/master/lib/security/ci_configuration/sast_build_action.rb#L24
Thanks. Let's proceed with this first.

issue_context.title: Cop idea: Redundant safe navigation for basic types
issue_context.body:
## Describe the solution you'd like

1. 
```ruby
hsh = [['a', '1'], ['b', '2']]
# hsh = nil

# bad
hsh&.to_h { |k, v| [k, v] } || {}
# bad
hsh&.to_h || {}

# good
hsh.to_h { |k,v| [k, v] }
# good
hsh.to_h
```

2.
```ruby
arr = ['a', 'b', 'c']
# arr = nil

# bad
arr&.to_a || []

# good
arr.to_a
```

3.
```ruby
str = "foo"
# str = nil

# bad
str&.to_s || ''

# good
str.to_s
```
comments: Rather than creating a new cop, extending the existing `Lint/RedundantSafeNavigation` can be considered. (I'm not yet convinced which is the better option.)
I do not think we need a new cop, `Lint/RedundantSafeNavigation` can be extended, as it was once extended for constants.

review_comments: It would be useful to document other literals as well.
